transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-07-20 08:30 PDT
- Duration: 47 minutes
- Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Miguel Torres (Redwood CSM), Jordan Blake (Meridian Lead PM), Samir Patel (Meridian Eng Mgr), Lee Huang (Meridian CTO), Rae Ortiz (Meridian Security)

Summary:
Meridian is evaluating Redwood for a customer-facing conversational feature in their analytics product. Primary concerns: time-to-first-call (speed to prototype), data residency/VPC, SOC2/KMS for secrets, latency vs cost tradeoffs for heavy read workloads, and an initial pilot with hosted sandbox credits. They asked for a short bench test with their prompt set to validate latency and cost. Redwood AE/SE explained self-serve onramp, free credits, and options (hosted API -> dedicated reserved -> private VPC). Next steps and owners at end.

Topics covered:
- Quickstart / free credits / time-to-first-call playbook
- Which deployment (hosted vs dedicated vs private) fits short pilot vs scale
- Security needs: SSO, SOC2, KMS/HSM, audit logs
- Performance: latency SLOs, batching, KV cache, quantization tradeoffs
- Bench plan and success criteria (latency p95, cost per 1k tokens, quality metrics)

Action items (captured in metadata above).

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for the time. I'm Alex, I'm the AE working with Priya here, SE. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Jordan Blake: Jordan here, Lead PM at Meridian. Samir, Lee, Rae on from our side.
[00:12] Samir Patel: Yep Samir.
[00:14] Lee Huang: Lee.
[00:16] Rae Ortiz: Rae, security.
[00:18] Priya Nair: Great, thanks. Real quick agenda: quickself-serve onramp, what hosting options look like for pilots, security checklist, and then map next steps. Sound good?
[00:28] Jordan: Perfect. Our goal is to get a beta of the assistant into our analytics dashboard within the next 3 weeks if possible. We want to see latency at p95 < 400ms for short queries and cost to be reasonable.
[00:38] Alex: Great, that's tight but doable depending on model choice and batching. Two quick questions before we dive: are you planning to run everything through a hosted sandbox initially or do you need a VPC from day one?
[00:48] Jordan: We wanted to try hosted to move fast, but security wants to understand VPC/private path. Rae, anything non-negotiable?
[00:56] Rae Ortiz: We need audit logs, SSO integration, and customer-managed keys for any PII. For pilot, hosted is ok if data is isolated and we have retention controls, but if we move to production, we likely need VPC or private plane — (sic) plane? private control plane.
[01:12] Priya: Understood. For hosted we provide tenant isolation, configurable retention, and you can opt into a private VPC later. Our typical flow is: self-serve API -> sandbox credits -> if pilot hits scale, upgrade to Dedicated reserved capacity -> Private if regulatory requires. There are some middle grounds like Dedicated in a shared VPC.
[01:30] Lee: Any SLA differences between hosted and dedicated?
[01:34] Alex: Yes. Hosted has best-effort SLAs for free tier, but production hosted customers get a baseline SLA; Dedicated comes with contractual SLOs for latency and uptime, and Private gets the highest isolation with enterprise terms. We can share exact SLA matrix — I'll send that after.
[01:48] Samir: For latency, we care about small queries where the text generation is short, but we also have some long-form summarization batches for nightly jobs. What's the recommendation here?
[01:58] Priya: For mixed workloads we suggest: small queries use a lower-latency model family, enable KV caching/prefix caching for repeated short contexts, and for nightly summarization consider a cost-optimized quantized variant or queued batch job on Dedicated. There's tuning knobs: max tokens, batch windows, and token streaming to the client.
[02:20] Jordan: You mentioned KV cache — how does that work with multi-tenant hosted? I worry about leakage or cross-tenant cache effects.
[02:28] Priya: Good question. The KV cache is per-request session and per-tenant in the hosted environment — it's not shared across tenants. Sometimes transcript transcribers call it "K-V cash" — it's not that. We persist session KV on the node to speed up autoregressive calls. For strict isolation we can also pin sessions to dedicated runner pools in Dedicated.
[02:50] Rae: Does hosted give us the option to manage our own KMS?
[02:54] Alex: By default hosted uses Redwood-managed encryption keys for convenience, but we offer a bring-your-own-key (BYOK) flow when you move to Dedicated or Private. For pilots we can enable stricter retention and audit logs; BYOK typically requires enterprise agreement but we can scope it.
[03:10] Samir: Ok good. Onboarding — how fast can we get to a first successful inference from our dev machine? We want to measure time-to-first-call (TTFC).
[03:20] Alex: For self-serve with free credits, most teams hit first successful call within an hour: signup, grab the API key, run the quickstart example. We'll also provide a Postman/insomnia collection and a small node/python snippet. The trickier part is instrumenting their prompt set and measuring latency/cost; that's where the bench test comes in.
[03:36] Jordan: That sounds right. We're evaluating a couple of prompts: short Q/A about analytics, and a 300-600 token summarize+insight generation. We'll share them.
[03:44] Priya: Perfect. We'll want those prompts to run against both a lower-latency model and a cost-optimized one so you can compare p95 and tokens per call. Suggestion: 100 samples each to start.
[03:55] Alex: Miguel from CSM will also send our onramp checklist and the free credit allocation details. Miguel?
[03:59] Miguel Torres: Yep I'll drop the sandbox creds and link to docs. Also including a short bench template you can run locally and a spreadsheet for capturing p50/p95 and cost-per-1k tokens.
[04:12] Jordan: Awesome. Rae — any immediate compliance blockers?
[04:15] Rae: We'll want to make sure the retention can be set to 30 days for pilot and that logs are available for audits. Also need to train the legal team on data processor relationships. Are you SOC2 Type II?
[04:27] Alex: We are SOC2 Type II; we'll attach the summary and the auditor report under NDA. We also provide role-based access controls in Console, SAML SSO integration, and audit logs. For Private deployments you can get an on-prem package or VPC private control plane.
[04:41] Lee: If we do Dedicated, what's the capacity commitment look like? We don't want to overprovision.
[04:47] Priya: Dedicated is typically reserved GPU capacity with monthly commit. We offer burst options and autoscaling policies to avoid wasted spend; and we can do shorter pilot commitments for POCs — e.g., 30-day trial of a small reserve. Pricing team will provide a tailored quote.
[05:02] Samir: On the model side: do you support open weights or only Redwood-curated models? We want to potentially bring our own fine-tuned models later.
[05:12] Priya: We support a model catalog with curated open models and tuned variants. For private deployments and Dedicated we can also host custom weights; there's an onboarding process for model ingestion and verifying perf/compat. For hosted we have vetted variants to balance latency/cost.
[05:28] Jordan: Any gotchas in the quickstart we should watch for? Like token counting surprises or streaming quirks?
[05:34] Alex: Token accounting can trip people up; we'll provide tooling to estimate tokens for your prompts. Also streaming can change client-side implementation; if you're doing server-sent events vs websockets we have samples. Priya, maybe share the batching guidance?
[05:45] Priya: Sure. For demo/prod parity: keep sequence lengths realistic, use prefix caching for repeated contexts, and enable small batch windows for low-latency paths. For bulk summarization, batch larger to improve throughput. There's a balance: bigger batches = better throughput but worse tail latency.
[06:02] Rae: For the BYOK flow, how long is the onboarding?
[06:06] Alex: BYOK onboarding is usually 2-4 weeks depending on legal/KMS integrations and any network peering for Private. For Dedicated we can sometimes expedite to 1-2 weeks if requirements are standard.
[06:16] Jordan: For the bench test, what dates can we aim for? We're hoping to run the bench and get results before our weekly product review next Friday.
[06:24] Alex: We can spin the sandbox creds today, Priya can prep a bench config. If you share prompts by Friday 07/23, we can run the bench early next week and present results by 07/29. Does that timeline work?
[06:36] Jordan: Yes that fits.
[06:38] Samir: A question about data residency — we have EU customers and need data to remain in eu-west region. Does hosted support region pinning?
[06:46] Priya: Hosted has region controls for data locality; we can route requests to eu-west nodes and metadata residency. For strict residency and control plane concerns, Private is the final solution.
[06:57] Rae: We also need SCIM and SSO.
[06:59] Alex: We support SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. We'll include config docs.
[07:06] Jordan: Pricing — are the free credits enough for a meaningful bench?
[07:10] Miguel: We typically issue sandbox credits that cover a few thousand short queries and a couple hundred longer summarization calls. If you need more we can bump it; we'll discuss the pilot pricing options after the bench.
[07:22] Samir: When you say "short queries"—can you give a token estimate?
[07:25] Priya: Short query is usually 20-80 tokens in prompt + 20-50 tokens in response. Summarization your 300-600 token inputs with 150-400 token outputs will be the heavy ones. We'll give cost estimates based on those numbers in the bench spreadsheet.
[07:40] Jordan: Any friction with our stack (we're node backend + k8s, using oauth for users)?
[07:45] Alex: None specific — our SDKs have node examples and you can call the REST API directly. For production you might want to run a small proxy or use our SDK with token rotation best-practices.
[07:55] Rae: Audit trails are critical. Will your logs show tokenized inputs? That may be sensitive.
[08:02] Priya: We can redact PII and optionally not persist full prompts for hosted. For pilot you can set retention and redaction; for strict guarantees we'd recommend Private. We'll document the options.
[08:12] Samir: For rate limiting and throttling, how do you handle spikes?
[08:16] Alex: We have per-account quotas and per-key rate limits. For Dedicated you get a predictable throughput and we can configure burst buffers. Also automatic fallback to smaller model or queueing is possible with routing policies.
[08:29] Jordan: Let's talk success criteria. For the product review we want: 1) run 100 short queries, p95 latency under 400ms in hosted eu-west; 2) run 50 summarizations, average cost per call below $0.70; 3) qualitatively similar outputs on both low-latency and cost-optimized models.
[08:48] Priya: Good concrete targets. We'll record them in the bench template. Also note that p95 depends on concurrency; we'll need to know your expected concurrent users to size the test.
[08:57] Samir: Expect ~30 concurrent requests at peak during beta.
[09:01] Priya: Okay we'll simulate 30 concurrency in the bench.
[09:05] Alex: Recap of next steps: Miguel sends creds + docs; Jordan sends prompts + priority SLOs; Priya prepares bench config and suggested settings (batch window, kv, model choices); Alex sends SOC2 summary + SLA matrix; schedule bench run and demo next week.
[09:20] Jordan: That sounds good. Anything else on the tech side?
[09:23] Lee: Quick question — how do you handle model rollouts? If we pin to a version and you push a model update, do we get notified?
[09:30] Priya: We support model pinning and controlled rollouts. You can pin model versions per-route and we have canary/A-B rollout mechanisms in the console. Notifications for deprecations and changes are part of our release cadence.
[09:43] Rae: Legal will want the data processing addendum — who signs that?
[09:46] Alex: We can share the DPA and standard terms; legal can sign after we get the pilot governance clarified.
[09:52] Jordan: Cool. If we like the bench results, expected transition to Dedicated would be in Q3.
[09:58] Alex: Great. Any final questions?
[10:00] Samir: One more tiny thing — do you have any example client-side code for streaming partial tokens and handling reconnection?
[10:06] Priya: Yes we'll include examples in JS/Go/python and a note on idempotency keys for retries.
[10:12] Jordan: Thanks everyone, this was helpful. We'll get the prompts and legal contact over.
[10:17] Alex: Thanks all — we'll follow up with the materials and a calendar invite for the bench run.
[10:22] Miguel: Sending creds after this call.
[10:25] Rae: Thanks.
[10:27] (call ends)

Notes about transcript quality: speakers occasionally overlapped; a few technical terms auto-transcribed incorrectly (e.g., "KV cash", "private plane" instead of private control plane). We preserved colloquial language and filler for realism.
